The business

Fauji Fertilizer Company is a listed fertilizer producer. Farmers’ demand, gas supply to the plants, and the regulated or negotiated price of product are the operating levers. It is a different business from an explorer that happens to produce gas, even when gas is the input.

The company is widely held and widely discussed as a dividend name. Discussion is not a declaration. Only the notice states the rate, the face value, and the dates. Between notices, the honest public sentence is that you should read the notice.

This page does not quote a live price, a dividend amount, or a target. Those figures belong in the company’s own notices, your broker, and — for a fund — the manager’s statement and MUFAP’s published NAV. PSX Tracker is not a broker and does not place orders.

Gas, subsidy, and cash

Fertilizer earnings can move with gas availability and with the treatment of subsidies or price decisions. Those are policy facts as much as factory facts. Read the director’s report for how the company described the year’s policy environment, and read the cash-flow statement to see whether the profit was collected.

A high accounting profit that does not become cash will show up as receivables or as another balance-sheet balance. That is the page to linger on.

In a personal ledger

If you own FFC for the dividend, your tracker still needs the purchases. The yield you care about is cash received against what you paid, after withholding, not a percentage someone quoted on a forum.

A face-value change, if one occurs, changes the meaning of a percentage dividend. Check the notice’s face value against the face value stored in your notes before you multiply.

Common questions

Does this page show the live FFC price?

No. Publishing a scraped quote would copy someone else’s market data. Open your broker for the price you can trade, or the app after you sign in, for the research view.

Is FFC a buy?

No. This site does not rank or recommend shares. Read the latest accounts and decide for yourself.

How should I record FFC I already own?

Enter each fill with its date, quantity, price, and fees, then reconcile the quantity to your broker or CDC statement. Dividends go in as dividends, not as new deposits.
